name: Solmere City (Silence-Zone)
summary: The capital of the Bright Kingdom, undone by its own harvest-blessing. A civic working tore a pocket of Quiet beneath the city; now it stands a day's walk from Velkash, perfect and silent, inside a treaty line no one crosses. Every Censer argument ends with 'remember Solmere.'
original_role: capital of Solmere, the Bright Kingdom (see factions/extinct-orders.json)

current_state.access: forbidden by the Accords of 184 AA; the treaty line is marked by white posts and Censer watchtowers
current_state.condition: buildings intact, colors unfaded within the zone; sound does not carry across the line and does not quite behave inside it
current_state.inhabitants: none confirmed. Birds circle the line and land elsewhere. Once a year, on the Backfiring's anniversary, every bell in Velkash rings once, unassisted.

sites.name: The Sunspire
sites.description: Solmere's temple to Solvane, still bright. Its great lens remains aimed at the sun; Veil-Wardens theorize the working is not broken but paused, mid-blessing.

sites.name: The Harvest Square
sites.description: Where the working was cast. The cobblestones bear a spiral crack that has not widened in 629 years — or has widened by exactly one hand's width, depending which survey is believed.

sites.name: The Treaty Posts
sites.description: White posts marking the Accords line, each carved with the names of the signatories. Someone leaves flowers at the nearest post every Stilleven; the Censer has stopped investigating who.

sites.name: The Open College
sites.description: Solmere's reopened college of the Weave, abandoned mid-lecture. Chalkboards still bear diagrams. The Censer burned the library in 184 AA; the cellars were never searched.

hazards: Sound dies at the line; travelers report their own footsteps continuing without them
The pocket of Quiet beneath the city is small but growing — Veil-Wardens measure it yearly against the treaty posts
Censer watchtowers every half-mile; crossers are taken, not killed, and 'taken' is worse
adventure_hooks: The Veil-Wardens' yearly survey needs discreet escorts: the measurement shows the pocket grew twice as fast this year
A Rememberer cell believes the Open College's cellars hold pre-Edict texts Solmere's scholars collected — the one library the Censer never catalogued
Who leaves the flowers? The answer intersects with House Dellet's sealed records in the Censer Quarter
